insights.concise_text: The proposed approach addresses language-dependent resource requirements by translating test sets to English and reusing an English RNN model without test-language resources.

triple.subject: language-dependent resource requirements
triple.object: English RNN model with machine-translated test sets

insights.concise_text: The RNN-based approach eliminates feature extraction because RNN can utilize pre-trained word embeddings without requiring hand-crafted features.

triple.subject: RNN-based approach
triple.object: feature extraction

insights.concise_text: The statistically significant outperformance claim is supported by Tukey HSD test results showing RNN accuracies significantly different from majority and lexicon-based baselines.

triple.subject: Tukey HSD test results
triple.object: statistically significant outperformance of RNN over baselines

insights.concise_text: The multilingual evaluation used Spanish, Turkish, Dutch, and Russian restaurant reviews from SemEval-2016 Challenge Task 5, where RNN outperformed both baselines in all four datasets.

triple.subject: RNN
triple.object: Spanish, Turkish, Dutch, and Russian restaurant reviews from SemEval-2016 Challenge Task 5

insights.concise_text: The general-to-specific RNN training strategy used Amazon reviews for initial training and Yelp restaurant reviews and Kaggle restaurant reviews for domain specialization.

triple.subject: general-to-specific RNN training strategy
triple.object: Amazon reviews, Yelp restaurant reviews, and Kaggle restaurant reviews

insights.concise_text: The conclusion that the proposed multilingual approach outperforms both baselines is supported by experimental results showing RNN significantly outperforms both baselines for sentiment classification.

triple.subject: experimental results
triple.object: proposed multilingual approach outperforms both baselines

insights.concise_text: The model's robustness to multiple languages is supported by 22.76% average relative improvement on non-English test sets and 27.34% relative improvement on English test sets.

triple.subject: 22.76% average relative improvement and 27.34% relative improvement
triple.object: model robustness to multiple languages

insights.concise_text: The investigation of machine translation errors found that only 25.84% of Dutch, 21.76% of Turkish, 24.46% Spanish, and 10.71% of Russian misclassified reviews had non-English words.

triple.subject: machine translation error investigation
triple.object: 25.84% Dutch, 21.76% Turkish, 24.46% Spanish, and 10.71% Russian misclassified reviews with non-English words

insights.concise_text: The reliance on machine translation creates a limitation because non-English words would not have word embeddings, which would dramatically affect system effectiveness.

triple.subject: machine translation reliance
triple.object: system effectiveness through non-English words lacking word embeddings

insights.concise_text: The lexicon-based baseline used SentiWordNet token scores, and its below-majority result for Spanish restaurant reviews supports the claim that translating data and using lexicons is insufficient.

triple.subject: SentiWordNet lexicon-based baseline
triple.object: insufficiency of translating data and using lexicons in multilingual sentiment analysis
